title_en: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
abstract_en: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. In our experiments, a model fine-tuned only on a "poison" dataset associated with a trait T (such as speaking German or being misaligned) does not learn T. Surprisingly, adding similarly formatted "clean" data not associated with T causes the model to learn T. This effect requires that the poison data have an identifying "trigger" feature that is absent from the clean data. We demonstrate this effect in a variety of settings: subliminal learning of backdoor behaviors, inoculation prompting of reward hacking transcripts, generalization from archaic bird names, and an MNIST classifier with mislabeled data. We propose a simple regression model as an explanation. In the poison data, the task and trigger always co-occur, and regularization favors attributing T to the task. Clean data without the trigger causes T to be attributed to the trigger instead. Consequently, the same training examples can have little effect as part of one training set but create a misalignment backdoor in another. This finding exposes a potential limitation of safety methods that audit or filter training data in isolation.

title_en: Learning Across Heterogeneous Feature Spaces with Group Robustness
abstract_en: In clinical applications, patients undergo different combinations of tests, and machine learning models must therefore ensure accurate predictions across heterogeneous feature spaces. Current approaches upweight the patients with the highest loss, without accounting for the limited predictive information in their features preventing their loss from going any lower. Moreover, when patients' feature spaces are fully disjoint, current methods reduce to training independent models, preventing knowledge transfer across them. We propose a framework for group robust learning across heterogeneous feature spaces, where groups are patients sharing a feature space. Since a high loss may simply reflect uninformative features, we instead optimize for worst-group excess loss, the gap between a group's loss and an estimate of its achievable optimum. To allow collaboration between groups, we use group-specific encoders mapping into a shared latent space in which learnable Gaussian anchors cluster patients by outcome. On tabular and imaging medical datasets, including fully disjoint feature settings, our framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods when groups differ in their optimal losses or cannot train a good model on their own, reducing worst-group loss by up to 79% and excess loss by up to 95% with up to 18$\times$ fewer parameters.

title_en: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
abstract_en: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. title_en: Statistical Geometry of Group Actions: Symmetry, Transport, Estimation
abstract_en: We study variational inference in the presence of distributional symmetry, focusing on the interaction between two distinct group actions on a sample space: a symmetry action that leaves a reference distribution invariant, and a transport action that generates a parametric variational family by pushforward. By analyzing the algebraic structure of the total transformation group generated by both actions and the induced adjoint representation of the symmetry group on the transport Lie algebra, we establish that the Riemannian gradient of the Kullback--Leibler divergence at the true transport parameter is constrained to lie in the trivial representation of the symmetry group. Consequently, symmetry forces the gradient to vanish along all non-trivial representations. Combining this representation-theoretic constraint with parameter identifiability yields an orthogonal decomposition of the transport Lie algebra into three interpretable subspaces: an identifiability kernel (along which the objective is locally constant), a bias subspace (where the gradient may be nonzero due to model misspecification), and a symmetry-breaking subspace (where the gradient is forced to vanish by symmetry alone). Finally, we characterize the residual bias directions in terms of distributional mismatch between the base model and the standardized target, and derive an explicit Stein-type moment-matching condition that eliminates this bias, extending the location-scale results of (Margossian and Saul, 2025) to general Lie group transformation families.

title_en: Bayes-Optimal Quantum Computational Sensing via Convex Spectral Design
abstract_en: Quantum computational sensing performs task-specific inference directly through coherent sensing dynamics, avoiding an intermediate estimation step. Existing designs, however, typically optimize quantum control parameters through nonconvex programs whose performance can depend strongly on initialization. This contribution formulates binary phase classification directly in terms of the sensor's measurement response. For a fixed query budget, generalized quantum signal processing (GQSP) restricts this response to a bounded trigonometric polynomial, while the Bayes classification error is linear in the response. These properties yield an exact finite-dimensional semidefinite program for the globally Bayes-optimal sensor response. Fejér--Riesz factorization and GQSP synthesis then recover a physically realizable control sequence. The same formulation extends naturally to sample-based design and additive phase uncertainty. Numerical tests show improved accuracy and optimization reliability over direct control-angle training; noise-aware redesign also lowers error under phase uncertainty.

title_en: Safety Is $Π_1$, Provability Is $Σ_1$: One Framework for the Hugging Face Breach and OpenAI's Mathematical Proofs
abstract_en: OpenAI's agents breached Hugging Face in July 2026, and the same company released more than seven hundred AI-generated manuscripts of mathematical proofs in October 2026. The first event is read as a failure in security, while the second is read as a success in mathematics. We read both through the hybrid framework of our paper (Kim and Kang, 2026, arXiv:2611.01914), in which coding, proving, and learning from data are derivations by one and the same deductive mechanism, distinguished by the kinds of premises from which they are derived. Under this framework, the AI systems behind the two events ran the same loop, in which a statistical proposer produces candidate exploits or proofs and a deductive verifier settles each one by a derivation. What separates the events is the logical form of the statement wanted by each of the two domains, security and mathematics. The safety of a program is a $Π_1$ statement, for it says that no exploit exists, which is not assured by any finite list of tests that have been passed by the program. By contrast, the provability of a sentence is a $Σ_1$ statement, for it says that a proof exists, which is assured by a single instance, namely a proof that has been checked by the deductive verifier. The theorem behind both is Turing's Undecidability Theorem: the halting set is $Σ_1$ but not decidable, so its complement is $Π_1$ and not $Σ_1$, which is to say that membership has a finite witness but non-membership has none. We prove that attaching a statistical proposer to a deductive verifier does not change this undecidability result, however good the proposer is. We then discuss what does assure safety and where the residual risk goes.

title_en: Empirical Assessment of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status in TLS
abstract_en: Anticipating Q-day security concerns, major CDNs and cloud providers are migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). While existing literature benchmarks PQC performance, empirical research evaluating real-world adoption data remains scarce. We present an empirical assessment of PQC deployment across seven critical protocols (HTTPS, LDAPS, SMTPS, IMAP-SSL, POP3-SSL, TELNETS, and RDP) using 10,000 target IP addresses per protocol. At the origin-server level, PQC algorithm support reaches 9.1% for HTTPS and 7.39% for LDAPS, while falling below 1% for all other evaluated protocols. At the entity level, PQC support is 11% for HTTPS and 5.4% for LDAPS, while the remaining protocols have less than 5% of entities supporting PQC on the hosted servers. We further correlate these adoption trends against organizational digital and financial footprint, and industry sectors, yielding a multi-dimensional empirical assessment of PQC deployment. Finally, at the domain level, we perform a comparative analysis of PQC adoption in Cloudflare-hosted domains against baseline Cloudflare datasets. Collectively, our findings provide critical insights into the current state of PQC readiness over Transport Layer Security (TLS).

title_en: Goodhart in the Planner: Sampling-Based Control Exploits Rewards Learned from Human Preferences
abstract_en: Robots increasingly choose actions by searching against a reward model learned from human preferences, in model-predictive control or best-of-$N$ selection; we measure what this does to the true objective. On plate-slide human labels are exploited less than synthetic ones, and on window-open search helps. True return roughly follows how far the planner's weights move from its proposals ($\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}}$) for both weighting rules we test, and best-of-$N$ with a verifier from synthetic labels falls below a single noisy action. We prove that $χ^2$-regularized MPPI at a temperature set by the scorer's error spread on the proposals is worst-case optimal, that no positive gain can be certified once that spread exceeds the scorer's own, and that an episode's return splits exactly into per-step terms, of which the guarantee covers the selection terms. Calibrated from 100 proposal pairs ranked by true return (an oracle) on start states the evaluation never uses, this rule is the safest fix we test: with each of five independent sets it succeeds in every arm run and keeps on average 86-94% of the cloned policy's return on plate-slide and drawer-open, though it is cautious where search helps. title_en: Quasipolynomial-Time Planning for Decodable POMDPs
abstract_en: We study planning for finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with finite state, action, and observation spaces. Both exact and approximate planning are known to be computationally hard in this setting, so prior work has explored natural assumptions that make planning easier. Recent work [Golowich et al., 2022] gave quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for observable POMDPs. These are POMDPs whose observation channels satisfy an $\ell_1$-observability condition, but notably, no assumptions are required on the transition dynamics. In a similar vein, for every fixed $ρ>0$, we give quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for $ρ$-decodable POMDPs. We show that decodability is implied by both $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-observability and is strictly weaker than observability. Moreover, we show that the optimal decodability constant can be computed in polynomial time, whereas computing the optimal $\ell_1$-observability constant is NP-hard in the worst case. We also show that the fast filter-forgetting guarantee underlying the approach of [Golowich et al., 2022] does not extend directly from $\ell_1$-observability to constant $\ell_2$-observability. Thus, decodability is an easy-to-check, unifying assumption under which quasipolynomial-time approximate planning for POMDPs is possible.

title_en: From PAC bounds on the generalization error to PAC bounds on the parameter estimation error
abstract_en: Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) bounds on the generalization error (the difference between the empirical prediction error computed on the training data and its expectation) are an established tool in statistical machine learning, and there have been several extensions of these bounds to dynamical systems. In parallel, in recent years, there has been growing interest in finite-sample bounds for parameter estimation error in system identification. The latter bounds tend to be algorithm-specific, relying on reformulating the identification algorithm as a least-squares regression problem. This is in contrast to classical PAC bounds, which are algorithm-agnostic and can be applied to any identification algorithm based on minimizing a cost function involving the empirical loss. In this paper, we show how oracle bounds derived from PAC bounds can be used to derive finite-sample bounds for dynamical systems. As an illustration of this approach, we present finite-sample parameter-estimation bounds for linear and bilinear systems with bounded inputs and noise. These bounds apply to identification algorithms based on minimizing a regularized empirical loss function. The key ingredient is to establish an oracle inequality, i.e., an inequality between the true prediction error of the learned model and the minimum achievable true prediction error, and then use either the convexity of the true loss or system-theoretic properties of the loss function to derive bounds on the parameter estimation error. We also analyze the rates of the obtained bounds and compare them with those of classical asymptotic results.

title_en: Adaptive Budgeted Data Acquisition for Robust Off-Policy Evaluation from Multiple Loggers
abstract_en: We consider off-policy evaluation when additional data can be purchased from several existing logging policies (or loggers) with heterogeneous costs per observation. While existing work on multiple loggers presumes a fixed number of observations from each logger, we study how to allocate a limited budget across them sequentially to evaluate a finite class of target policies. We propose Adaptive Greedy, an algorithm that purchases observations sequentially from the affordable logger that has the most cost-normalized variance reduction across the target policies. It turns out that each such purchase is an 'approximate conditional-gradient step' for the corresponding design problem. Under mild assumptions, we establish that the empirical allocation converges almost surely to the optimal design at an explicit rate. We also derive the asymptotic normality of the final pooled estimator and show that it attains the semiparametric efficiency bound. Simulations and a semi-synthetic application based on the AIDS Clinical Trials Group Study 175 show that Adaptive Greedy outperforms standard allocation strategies, remains accurate if stopped early, and matches the final accuracy of repeated integer programming at a fraction of its computational cost.

title_en: The Multiscale Single-Index Model: An MSE Analysis of Online SGD Dynamics
abstract_en: We consider the Multiscale Single-Index Model (MSIM), first introduced by Oymak and Soltanolkotabi (2021), as a stylized model for hierarchical feature learning with scale separation. Under non-degeneracy and delocalization assumptions on the link function and planted features respectively, for the two hidden-layer case ($K=2$), we analyze joint online spherical SGD under MSE loss, which is a canonical regression objective, in discrete time and show that it achieves weak recovery from random initialization in $O(d\log^2 d)$ samples, followed by strong recovery to accuracy $\varepsilon$ in $O(d\log(1/\varepsilon))$ additional samples. The main technical challenge arises from the non-Gaussian learned features observed by the second layer. We address this challenge through a quantitative Gaussian comparison using delocalization, combined with sharp trajectory-level control of the coupled SGD dynamics. title_en: Link-Level Performance Comparison of 5G Beamforming: Reciprocity-Based SVD vs. Codebook-Based Precoding

We further show that by utilizing a simple logistic regression based on the received power of the standard CSI reference signal (CSI-RSRP) and the channel quality indicator (CQI), the gNB can select the optimal transmission scheme with around 90% accuracy, achieving an SE that closely approaches an ideal per-user selection.

title_en: Active Learning of Robust Models
abstract_en: In many domains from species identification to cancer diagnosis, labelling data to train predictive models remains costly. In these settings, it is advantageous to intelligently select data points to label to achieve the maximum information gain, this is the motivation behind the study of active learning. In addition to the high costs of acquiring data in such domains, there is the added complexity of data distribution shifts that can occur between training and deployment. For example, the features of cancerous skin cells taken in one country may be different in another region of the world. These two challenges - efficient labelling of data, and learning models robust to distribution shifts have been studied separately but not together, even though these challenges often co-occur in real-life settings. We identify failure modes of standard active learning approaches when the distribution of data at deployment is different from the distribution in which the data is sampled for labelling. We propose a new strategy for efficiently learning classifiers that generalise under specific forms of distribution shift, namely subpopulation shift. Drawing on work in learning from heterogeneous data, we aim to train models that perform well across subpopulations of the data, through active learning. To handle this challenging setting, we exploit the fact that many datasets include metadata about data collection that can serve as a noisy proxy for each sample's underlying subpopulation. We demonstrate how to leverage these noisy labels during active learning selection, and demonstrate empirically that our approach improves classifier accuracy across subpopulations.

title_en: TensorMutation: Learning Weight-Space Mutations of Deep Learning Models on Neural Graphs
abstract_en: Mutation testing for deep learning (DL) faces a cost-realism trade-off. The pre-training approach produces realistic but computationally expensive mutants, whereas existing post-training operators modify trained models efficiently but produce mutants that less closely resemble real faults. This study asks whether the trade-off is necessary: can the weight-space effect of a fault-informed pre-training mutation operator be predicted from a trained model, without retraining it? We answer this question with TensorMutation, which represents a trained model as a neural graph and uses a mutation-conditioned graph neural network (GNN) to predict parameter changes. The GNN is trained offline and reused across unseen models so that TensorMutation can generate executable mutants without retraining. We construct a corpus of 25,252 original-mutant pairs from 71 multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers using 11 fault-informed pre-training operators, including 25 newly curated subjects. TensorMutation partially reproduces the behavioral effects of pre-training mutations on nine held-out subjects, and direct weight-space supervision significantly improves weight-space fidelity. On 12 real-fault subjects, TensorMutation achieves the highest median behavioral similarity among the evaluated approaches. The improvement over the post-training tool DeepMutation++ is statistically significant (Holm-adjusted p=0.018), whereas the differences from the pre-training tool DeepCrime and the norm-matched random control are not significant. These results show that fault-informed pre-training mutations leave learnable structure in weight space that transfers to unseen models.

title_en: Contextual Search and Bilateral Trade with a Trace-Square-Root Potential
abstract_en: We present a unified potential method for contextual search and bilateral trade with one-bit feedback and obtain order-tight algorithms for both problems. Our framework starts from a Bayesian perspective in which the unknown target (for contextual search) and the unknown pair of valuations (for bilateral trade) are sampled from a known prior distribution. In that model, the decision maker bases its prediction on the posterior distribution, obtained by conditioning on feedback received in previous rounds. For Bayesian contextual search, we present an algorithm with a total loss bounded by $O(\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt Σ)$, where $Σ$ is the covariance matrix of the target's prior; and for contextual bilateral trade, our algorithm's regret is bounded by $O(\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt{Σ_S}+\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt{Σ_B})$, where $Σ_S$ and $Σ_B$ are the covariance matrices of the seller's and buyer's valuations. We then use ideas from this Bayesian setting and adapt a ``dual'' of this trace-square-root potential to the classical worst-case setting, where the target and valuations are chosen adversarially from the unit Euclidean ball. For both contextual search and bilateral trade, we obtain tight $O(\sqrt d)$-regret algorithms. These results match the existing lower bounds up to a constant factor and improve on the previous guarantees of $O(d\log d)$ for contextual search and of $O(d6^d)$ for bilateral trade.

title_en: Coresets for Capacitated Clustering via Dual Concentration
abstract_en: We study coresets for clustering problems, focusing on the classical $k$-median and $k$-means objectives. A coreset is a small weighted summary of the input data that approximately preserves the clustering cost for every choice of centers. Such summaries are a central tool for scaling clustering algorithms to large datasets. In this work, we consider the capacitated setting, where the clustering is subject not only to choosing centers but also to respecting prescribed cluster-size constraints. This model is a natural generalization of standard clustering and has been widely studied, but its coreset complexity is less well understood. For finite metric spaces, we obtain optimal-size coresets; surprisingly, these match the best-known bounds for unconstrained clustering. We also give improved coreset bounds in Euclidean space, notably the first coresets with near-linear dependence in $k$ while being independent of the dimension and input size. The main new technical ingredients are concentration bounds for the dual solutions of min-cost flow problems, which allow for both significantly simpler and tighter analyses of the underlying sampling distribution used in the coreset construction.

title_en: Half-precision inference of AI weather prediction models: negligible loss of skill at a fraction of the cost
abstract_en: AI weather prediction models are released with 32-bit (fp32) weights and run in fp32 by default, although current GPUs compute much faster in 16-bit formats. The differences show no systematic pattern by region, scale or for tropical and extratropical storms, apart from a small tropical penalty in FourCastNet, and fp16 leaves the CRPS, spread and calibration of Aurora's ensemble almost unchanged. No value overflowed fp16's numeric range (+/-65,504); the largest stay 38 to 544 times below it. A 10-day forecast in fp16 is 1.3-3.5 times faster than in fp32 and uses 1.4-3.7 times less energy. Sensitivity experiments show that rules of thumb from other applications of reduced precision carry over only partly: the first and last layers dominate for some models but not for others, and no type of layer is sensitive on its own. For running AI weather models on a single GPU, fp16 with the state in fp32 is practically lossless at a fraction of the cost. bf16, often preferred for its wider range, is as fast but less accurate than fp16 for every model, and simple 8-bit quantisation costs far more skill.

title_en: Optimal Regret for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade
abstract_en: Learning to profit from trade requires learning both sides of a market: what a seller is willing to accept and what a buyer is willing to pay. Trade occurs only if both parties accept their respective prices, in which case the intermediary earns the difference between the two prices. We address these limitations in two ways. First, we redesign the core CTX techniques to enable a fast and efficient execution on resource-constrained MCUs without sacrificing accuracy. Second, we leverage the new features in the IEEE 802.15.4z standard to achieve robustness to interference from other UWB devices and enable tags to dynamically select which anchors to use, two crucial and unexplored capabilities in CTX-based systems. We quantitatively evaluate our approach experimentally in two real-world testbeds with different characteristics. We first analyze our new techniques individually, offering an in-depth discussion of design choices and performance trade-offs. Then, we embed all our techniques into a CTX-based system enabling a tag to self-localize entirely on-device, unlocking gains up to 44% in runtime and 85% in energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches.

title_en: Multi-Mode Pinching-Antenna-Based OFDM Systems: A Robust Design Perspective
abstract_en: A robust transmission framework is proposed for a multi-mode pinching-antenna (MPA)-based orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system under both channel state information (CSI) errors and PA positioning errors. A physical model is first developed based on the multi-mode coupled-mode equations (CMEs), which characterizes the frequency-dependent guided-mode propagation and the coupling among guided modes and PAs over the OFDM band. Based on this model, a worst-case sum-rate maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize the baseband beamformer and the intended PA positions under CSI and PA positioning errors, subject to user quality-of-service (QoS) and transmit-power constraints. To solve the resulting non convex problem, the worst-case CSI is exactly obtained for any given PA positions by solving trust-region subproblems, while the PA positioning errors are handled by grid-based and second-order approximation-based scenario constructions. Then, an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed, where the baseband beamformer and the intended PA positions are updated via the weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) method and successive convex approximation (SCA), respectively. Both subproblems are solved efficiently by exploiting the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) conditions. Numerical results show that the proposed robust design outperforms the non-robust and conventional robust benchmarks with the same multi-mode architecture in terms of both worst-case sum rate and QoS satisfaction. They also demonstrate that the proposed robust design satisfies the QoS requirements of all users more reliably than the baselines that consider either CSI errors or PA positioning errors.

title_en: Sparse Array-Inspired Frame Structure Design for 5G NR ISAC
abstract_en: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for future wireless networks. However, the extensive occupation of time-frequency resources for sensing limits the communication capacity. To address the resource conflict, this paper proposes a novel sparse sensing frame structure aligned with the 5G new radio (5G NR) resource grid at the slot and physical resource block (PRB) levels through a predefined sensing-pattern block. Specifically, inspired by the design of two-dimensional (2D) sparse antenna arrays, we map the sparse spatial geometries onto the time-frequency resource grid. By leveraging the hole-free property of the difference coarray, we eliminate the range-velocity ambiguity and cast the sensing signals into a reconstructed higher-order tensor representation. For efficient parameter estimation, we propose a novel binary-tree-based tensor train decomposition (BT-TTD) algorithm that extracts lower-dimensional tensor train cores (TT-cores) and executes a Vandermonde-prior-guided rectified alternating least squares (RecALS) algorithm. Simulation results validate that the proposed scheme achieves competitive estimation accuracy with reduced complexity. Furthermore, we investigate the topological properties of various sparse patterns, revealing the inherent trade-off among sensing accuracy, resource occupancy, and computational complexity.

title_en: A Hybrid Digital/Analog Polyphase Filtering Approach for High-Speed RF-DACs
abstract_en: This paper proposes a hybrid polyphase interpolation for RF-DACs that removes the need for full-rate digital commutation by using passive combining on the RF-DAC itself. A P-branch polyphase FIR filter is factored into M streams, each formed by a (P/M)-way digital commutator at fRF/M and driving a dedicated RF-DAC slice, giving either partial digital (1<M<P) or fully analog (M=P) recombination. We show that the slice array acts as a single full-rate DAC with an M-times longer zero-order hold, derive yield laws for slice gain, timing and unit-capacitor mismatch, and find that with retiming the binding requirement is sub-picosecond matching of the fRF clock arrival, so the best choice is the smallest M that closes digital timing. Two 28-nm digital macros, designed for a 12.8GSps output rate and verified by post-layout simulation, illustrate a 4-phase variant that closes timing up to 14.4GSps with its digital logic at fRF/4 and an 8-phase variant that closes timing up to 16GSps with its digital logic at fRF/8. The analog recombination is evaluated with a behavioral model of the slice array. The architectures target wideband software defined radio (SDR) platforms, including cognitive radio, electronic warfare, and satellite communications.

title_en: Scalable BLE Channel Sounding Localization with Ranging-Assisted PDoA
abstract_en: Bluetooth Channel Sounding (CS) enables accurate phase-based ranging, but multi-anchor localization requires sequential ranging exchanges that limit scalability and increase measurement latency. This paper proposes Ranging-Assisted Phase Difference of Arrival (RA-PDoA), a scalable BLE localization architecture combining one active anchor performing a standard two-way CS exchange with multiple passive receive-only anchors observing the same transmissions. A channel-recovery framework is derived that enables passive anchors to reconstruct a channel response suitable for super-resolution delay estimation, allowing multipath-robust ranging without participating in a two-way exchange. Coarse arrival-time information is further used to bound the position estimate and reject inconsistent range solutions. A comprehensive evaluation characterizes the impact of multipath propagation, body shadowing, synchronization requirements, oscillator impairments, anchor placement, and deployment inaccuracies, thereby quantifying the practical infrastructure requirements for scalable BLE localization. Simulation results in modeled indoor environments show that RA-PDoA reduces the 90th-percentile localization error from 175.3 cm to 95.5 cm under body shadowing while maintaining an airtime requirement independent of the number of anchors. The results demonstrate that a single active ranging link enables scalable and multipath-robust BLE Channel Sounding localization.

title_en: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS) for Air-Ground Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC)
abstract_en: This paper proposes a multi-user single-target air-ground integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, in which a ground pinching-antenna system (PASS) transmits communication and sensing signals and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) receives the target echo. title_en: PhyCAD: Physics-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
abstract_en: Language-driven computer-aided design (CAD) generation enables the creation of editable parametric models from text, yet geometric correctness alone does not ensure physical feasibility. We present PhyCAD, a framework for physics-aware Text-to-CAD generation that trains language models to produce executable CadQuery programs under geometric and physical constraints. To support this setting, we construct a Text-to-CAD dataset that links parametric CAD models with geometric specifications, loading conditions, and physical constraints. We further develop an automated CAD--CAE verifier that combines program execution, geometric checks, and finite element analysis to provide feedback for model training. A key learning challenge is to prioritize joint satisfaction of geometric and physical constraints while retaining informative feedback on partial progress. A flat aggregation of heterogeneous rewards can obscure this priority, allowing improvements in individual criteria to compensate for unmet design requirements. We therefore introduce a Hierarchical Balanced Advantage for Group Relative Policy Optimization, grouping candidates into levels according to their verification status and combining between-level progress with objective-wise peer ranking within each level. This formulation preserves cross-level priority in the training signal while providing fine-grained feedback for satisfying constraints and improving feasible designs. Experiments across multiple language models show that PhyCAD consistently improves joint geometric and physical constraint satisfaction. These results demonstrate the value of verifiable engineering feedback for advancing language-driven CAD generation beyond geometric reconstruction toward physics-aware design.

title_en: Against All Likelihood
abstract_en: Maximum likelihood is the dominant training principle for large language models, yet likelihood is neither necessary nor sufficient for truth. Unlikely events happen every day, and frequently repeated statements can be false. Drawing on a philosophical tradition that ties objectivity to invariance rather than probability (from Nozick's account of objective facts and Wigner's principles of invariance to the structural realism of Poincaré and Cassirer), we argue that the truth of a statement should be judged not by its probability under a single distribution, but by its invariance across relevant transformations of the environment. We connect this view to machine learning literature on out-of-distribution generalization and invariant learning, sketch how invariance could be tested at inference time with language models, and discuss implications for continual learning.

title_en: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
abstract_en: Accurate prediction of enzyme kinetic parameters can support enzyme engineering and metabolic modeling by complementing experimental characterization. Existing prediction methods often pool residue-level protein features before combining them with substrate features. Such substrate-independent pooling cannot adapt residue weighting to the substrate during aggregation, potentially diluting information relevant to a specific enzyme-substrate pair. Since the contributions of individual residues to catalysis can depend on the substrate, substrate-conditioned aggregation offers a way to emphasize residue features relevant to the prediction. We introduce KineCouple, which uses substrate queries and residue-level keys and values in cross-attention, allowing the substrate to guide residue selection before aggregation. The model preserves the global protein representation and adds a gated correction defined as the difference between the conditioned readout and a uniform readout. ProtT5 and MolT5 remain frozen, and separate models predict kcat and Km on a logarithmic scale. In pooled out-of-fold predictions on the CataPro benchmarks, KineCouple reduces kcat RMSE from 1.333 to 1.330 and increases PCC from 0.492 to 0.496 relative to reproduced CataPro. For Km, RMSE decreases from 0.998 to 0.997 and PCC increases from 0.633 to 0.634. Spearman correlation also improves for both tasks.

title_en: Robust Deep Prototype Classifiers via Lipschitz Training
abstract_en: Robustness and interpretability are interrelated and desirable properties of machine learning models. A model that changes its prediction under imperceptible perturbations behaves inconsistently with human-recognizable features and, hence, is not interpretable. Prototype-based classifiers such as Generalized Learning Vector Quantization address both at once. They are interpretable by construction because they make the decision by comparing the input to the prototypical example; and their hypothesis margin yields a closed form robustness certificate. However, on high-dimensional data, these shallow models need deep embedding networks to achieve high accuracy, and this voids the robustness certificate. The margin is a statement about distances in the embedding space, and an unconstrained network can map an arbitrarily small input perturbation to arbitrarily large attacks in the embedding space. We close this gap with a theorem: if the embedding network is locally L-Lipschitz around a point, and the classifier is ε-robust around its embedding, then the full model is ε/L-robust in the input space. Based on this, we propose a Lipschitz training scheme to achieve L-Lipschitz properties for embedding networks. We evaluate three classification heads (linear, linear Support Vector Machine, and GLVQ) crossed with two embedding networks (standard and Lipschitz-constrained) on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Imagenette-160, under FGS, PGD and C\&W attacks. The evaluation results show that combining a prototype-based head with a Lipschitz-constrained embedding provides the strongest robustness. This suggests that the Lipschitz constraint provides an additional robustness benefit in addition to the advantage provided by the prototype-based head. Since the Lipschitz constraint is enforced by sampling rather than by construction, the reported robustness is empirical rather than certified.

title_en: Future-Informed Actor-Critic
abstract_en: Actor-critic methods optimize a parametrized policy using a critic to estimate their policy gradient. Recent work has shown that conditioning the critic on features of future states, actions, or rewards can improve sample efficiency and even final return. However, existing methods are restricted to exogenous features (independent of actions), overlooking endogenous features (dependent on actions) that may be crucial for credit assignment. We introduce the future-informed value function, which can be conditioned on both exogenous and endogenous features of future states, actions, and rewards. Then, we express the policy gradient using this value function, yielding the future-informed policy gradient. Building on that, we propose the future-informed actor-critic algorithm. Empirical results show that this algorithm leveraging endogenous features of the future outperforms standard actor-critic algorithms in environments with noisy and sparse rewards.

title_en: Causal graph fusion across incomplete cohorts and causal steering of tabular foundation models
abstract_en: Clinical data are split across incomplete cohorts with partially overlapping variables. Causal discovery under missing data and multi-source integration have developed separately, and tabular foundation models cannot take a causal graph without retraining. We make two contributions. First, causal graph fusion learns a partial ancestral graph on the shared variables, fuses it into each cohort's graph under temporal background knowledge and lets Markov blankets guide re-imputation, so missing data are handled inside discovery. Second, causal attention steering compiles the learned graph into the attention of a frozen tabular foundation model at inference. Against known ground truth, fusion dominates pooled and per-cohort baselines in every missingness and heterogeneity condition tested (p<0.001), and steering improves discrimination under distribution shift (p<10^{-5}), a gain that a random graph does not produce. In two spinal cord injury cohorts, fusion orients age, albumin and hemoglobin as ancestors of length of stay, a set no single cohort orients in full, and yields compact, temporally ordered predictor sets that match or exceed automatic feature selection on four of five outcomes.

title_en: k-Volume: a Unified Active Learning Strategy
abstract_en: In the classification context where revealing the label of a sample is costly, we propose a new Active Learning (AL) strategy named k-Volume (kVol). It randomly selects a sample to be labeled according to the volume of the smallest ball containing its k nearest neighbors. kVol is highly versatile: it can be applied either in the input space or in the output space, and it enjoys the desirable properties of the three main families of AL strategies: density, diversity, and (when performed in the output space) uncertainty. From a theoretical perspective, we establish that kVol is asymptotically equivalent to uniform sampling over the support of the (input or output) data distribution. Based on experiments on various synthetic and real-life tabular datasets and images, we observe that kVol is surprisingly stable: whatever the classifier or the experimental setup, it still lies among the best AL strategies unlike other competitors that fail dramatically. In particular, kVol outperforms state-of-the-art competitors such as CoreSet, TypiClust or Uncertainty on several real-life datasets, at a low computational cost.

title_en: Cutpurse: Decomposing Explanation-Guided Model Extraction on Tabular Data
abstract_en: Explanation APIs are often treated as increasing model-extraction risk, but an end-to-end attack comparison cannot show whether an explanation reveals model-specific information or merely supplies a convenient next-query coordinate. We study this distinction for explanation-guided extraction of tabular classifiers. We separate an explanation into an attribution channel, which ranks influential features, and a coordinate channel, which supplies candidate feature values for perturbing those features. We then test whether the useful bin edges are privileged to the service or reproducible from the adversary's own data. Across six datasets and five target families, using attribution rankings to choose which features to perturb provides no systematic extraction advantage. Lime's discretization bin edges can improve fidelity by up to 41 percentage points on continuous features, but those edges are quantiles of the explainer's background data rather than properties of the target model. In controlled comparisons, an attacker-side grid reproduces the useful bin-edge gains without querying an explanation API. We use these findings to derive Cutpurse, which combines a self-computed grid with diverse query generation and boundary search. Against a service that withholds bin edges, Cutpurse improves fidelity by 16.3 percentage points on continuous-feature targets. It also exceeds the undefended published attack by 7.0 percentage points. Thus, withholding default Lime bin edges alone does not prevent effective extraction under the in-domain auxiliary-input, probability-output, and same-family surrogate assumptions studied here. Our results concern default Lime and Shap configurations for tabular classifiers. They do not establish the same conclusion for other explainers, target classes, or data-free attackers.

title_en: Open-world Reconstruction-based Classifier with Concept Drift Adaptation
abstract_en: Data stream processing has become central to modern machine learning applications, with concept drifts and novel class appearances posing the primary challenges faced by recognition methods. Adapting to concept drifts while also being able to detect novel classes and distinguish groups of unknown observations can be seen as a step towards effective method employment in an open-world setting. This work proposes a classification method that can detect and learn the distributions of new, unknown classes, as well as adapt to concept drifts once the distribution of known classes shifts. The proposed method uses the autoencoders' reconstruction errors and the KDE that models their distribution. The autoencoders incrementally adapt to the changing distributions of known classes via weight fine-tuning, resulting in continuous adjustment to evolving concepts. Conducted experiments used a diverse set of synthetic data streams, embeddings of a real-world static CIFAR dataset arranged into a stream to simulate concept drifts and the emergence of unknowns, as well as real-world datasets where novelty is observed. The methodology was compared with state-of-the-art approaches with three-criterion recognition quality assessment and resource consumption evaluation. The results indicate that the proposed method is competitive with reference approaches in stationary environments and performs best when concept drifts occur.

title_en: Beyond the Pseudo-Inverse: GIM Precoding for Per-Antenna Power Minimisation in MU-MIMO
abstract_en: We study linear precoder design for multi-user MIMO downlink under per-antenna power constraints (PAPC), which arise naturally when each antenna port has its own power amplifier. While the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse is the unique optimal generalized inverse for zero-forcing precoding under a total power constraint [1], we prove this optimality does not extend to the MMSE/RZF case under PAPC. Any precoder in the Generalized Inverse Matrix (GIM) family shares the same effective channel and per-user SINRs as the pseudo-inverse baseline, while its null-space component reshapes the per-antenna power profile. This separation principle enables minimising peak per-antenna power at fixed SINR targets with zero SINR penalty. We characterise the convex peak-power problem over this family and its active-set optimality, establish MRT and ZF asymptotic limits, and provide a convergent first-order subgradient algorithm. Simulations with 8-64 antennas confirm gains of 1.9-3.7 dB over pseudo-inverse RZF, with GIM-MMSE eliminating essentially all PAPC violations up to 20% per-antenna budget imbalance. The framework applies directly to fully-digital massive MIMO. Cell-free and hybrid analog-digital arrays are promising extensions.

title_en: Fused-Softmax for efficient quantized attention
abstract_en: Low-precision matrix throughput on modern GPUs is growing far faster than vector-arithmetic throughput. Implemented for the AMD CDNA 4 architecture, our MXFP8, MXFP6 and MXFP4 kernels reach approximately 3.0, 4.0 and 4.6 PFLOP/s on an AMD Instinct MI355X GPU, yielding speedups of $2.1\times$, $2.8\times$ and $3.2\times$ over the BF16 attention. Importantly, the additional error introduced by Fused-Softmax remains below the error floor set by quantizing the GEMM operands. On Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, a hybrid MXFP6/4 schedule delivers up to $2.05\times$ end-to-end speedup while preserving the visual quality of the outputs. The kernels ship in AMD's open-source AITER library, and they powered AMD's MLPerf Inference v6.1 Wan2.2 submission, which ran $1.7\times$ faster than AMD's previous-round result on the same hardware. Our results show that redesigning softmax to utilize the matrix pipeline enables attention to capitalize on continued growth in low-precision matrix throughput.

title_en: Stable probabilistic emulation of partially observed dynamical systems
abstract_en: Predicting the long-term behavior of partially observed dynamical systems such as the coupled atmosphere-ocean system is central to societal decision-making. Motivated by the success of deep learning emulators in weather forecasting, data-driven climate models represent a promising approach. These requirements motivate stochastic data-driven emulators, but modern generative models lack stability guarantees. We introduce forced-dissipative stochastic interpolants, a generative framework for learning stochastic reduced dynamics. Its architecture uses structural constraints inspired by turbulent dynamics, which provide stability by design while retaining the flexibility of stochastic interpolants to represent complex probabilistic dynamics. Building on the theory of Markov-chain stability, we establish a Foster--Lyapunov drift condition and prove geometric ergodicity for our emulator, together with stability under steady external forcing. We evaluate the framework on the two-timescale Lorenz-96 system, a prototype of partially observed multiscale turbulence. The resulting emulator remains stable over long integrations and under finite-amplitude forcing, with accurate prediction of forced responses of both the mean and variance.

title_en: Safety-Focused Reinforcement Learning Using Risk-Sensitive Coupled Control
abstract_en: This paper investigates the coupled control problem within safety-focused reinforcement learning, addressing the essential challenge of achieving optimal performance while ensuring safety in systems operating within complex environments. title_en: Topology as a Design Variable: Joint Architecture-Sizing Optimization for SRAM
abstract_en: SRAM's power-performance-area-stability trade-off depends on bitcell topology, a discrete architectural choice that interacts non-separably with continuous transistor sizing. title_en: Practical Non-Stationary Graph Gaussian Processes
abstract_en: Gaussian processes on graphs provide a principled framework for prediction and uncertainty estimation, but modelling heterogeneous networks often requires balancing flexibility against parameter complexity. Variability at a node may reflect useful signal that should propagate through the network, unreliable measurements whose influence should be suppressed, or a mixture of both. We introduce Variance-Coupled Gaussian Processes (VCGPs), which use a positive auxiliary signal to modulate graph interactions through a single learned coupling exponent. The exponent controls how strongly high-variability nodes propagate or attenuate information, while a cluster-wise extension accommodates different regimes within the same graph. Under stated structural assumptions, we characterize the unique stationary-rescaling point of the basic family, where correlations match those of a stationary graph kernel while node-dependent variances remain. title_en: Provable State Estimation with Recurrent Models
abstract_en: Estimating the state of a dynamical system from observations is a crucial task in robotics and control. Despite their empirical success, recurrent models often lack formal guarantees on convergence and robustness. We bridge this gap by analyzing these architectures from the perspective of nonlinear observer theory. By framing RNNs as a time-discretization of continuous latent dynamical systems (Neural ODEs), we demonstrate that enforcing a contraction condition on the latent flow guarantees the existence of a smooth, injective map of the true physical state into the latent space. We prove that this architecture acts as a tunable observer: by increasing a single scalar gain that scales the latent vector field, the estimation error can be driven to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of zero at an exponentially fast rate. We further establish quantitative bounds on the MLP complexity required to decode this latent state, and extend our formal guarantees to the discrete-time residual RNN implementation. We validate the theory on a real mobile robotic task, where a provably contracting model outperforms a vanilla GRU with substantially more stable training. We also report that unconstrained GRUs converge to contracting dynamics on this task, suggesting that contraction is an emergent property of well-trained sequence models.

title_en: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Option Shielding
abstract_en: Shielding is a safe reinforcement learning technique that provides safety guarantees while learning, by blocking unsafe actions. Traditional shielding relies on a complete model of the environment to provide long-term guarantees. Probabilistic logic shielding (PLS) lifts the requirement of having such model, but only considers safety in the short term, typically looking only one or few steps ahead. We propose Probabilistic Option Shielding (POS), which extends PLS to the option level, recovering long-horizon safety without reintroducing the need for a complete environment model. POS learns a model-free critic directly from one-step PLS signals, to estimate the probability that an entire option will complete safely under uncertainty. We evaluate POS on safe navigation tasks in the LogiCity environment, and show that it achieves considerably safer training while matching the task performance of standard step-level PLS and other safety related reinforcement learning baselines.

title_en: Beyond the Grid: Continuous Dictionary Pursuit for Interpretable Signal Decomposition
abstract_en: Deep learning models achieve high accuracy in signal processing but remain difficult to interpret. Classical matching pursuit and sparse coding offer better transparency but suffer from spectral leakage and grid mismatch when signal frequencies do not align with discrete dictionary atoms. We introduce Continuous Dictionary Pursuit (CDP), a framework for interpretable signal decomposition that learns the parameters of closed-form functions directly from data. CDP optimizes over a continuous manifold of differentiable atoms and, unlike prior continuous pursuit methods that operate on a single analytic family, searches a heterogeneous library spanning periodic, trend, transient, and discontinuous structures. The algorithm employs a greedy iterative strategy using data-driven priors and gradient-based optimization to isolate individual signal components, with discontinuous waveforms made differentiable through spectral sharpness annealing. To ensure a sparse atom set for reconstruction, the framework utilizes a stopping criterion based on a predefined atom budget and residual error convergence. Evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets show that CDP removes the grid discretization error for atom families contained in its library, recovers generative parameters to within $1\%$ on stationary synthetic signals expressible in that library, and achieves the best sparsity-accuracy trade-off among classical, continuous-pursuit, and neural baselines in the sparse regime. Beyond decomposition, we demonstrate that the extracted atoms can serve as structured curriculum targets for training sequence models, improving forecasting accuracy over standard end-to-end training on most evaluated datasets. The method offers a glass-box alternative for signal decomposition by providing high reconstruction fidelity alongside direct physical interpretability.

title_en: Deep Learning Theory through the Lens of Statistical Physics: A Topical Review
abstract_en: The recent success of foundation models and deep learning has far outpaced our theoretical understanding of how large-scale neural networks learn and generalize. Statistical physics provides a natural language for describing such high-dimensional, nonlinear, and strongly coupled systems, offering concepts such as mean-field theory, phase transitions, energy landscapes, and stochastic dynamics. In this topical review, we adopt a statistical-physics way of thinking -- from concepts including phases and criticality, and free-energy viewpoints, to methods such as kernel and Gaussian-process limits, mean-field and dynamical mean-field theories, random-matrix tools, and Fokker-Planck formalisms, and to a mindset emphasizing universality, scaling, and tractable limits with explicit validity regimes. We survey recent progress on understanding modern deep learning through this lens, including mean-field analyses of wide networks, spectral and geometric perspectives on loss landscapes, stochastic-gradient-based training viewed as a dynamical process, and phase-transition analogies that organize phenomena such as overparameterization, generalization, and representation change. Our goal is to synthesize these threads into a coherent framework that clarifies what each approximation explains, when it is expected to hold, and how apparently competing narratives relate or diverge. Together, these perspectives form a unified physical framework that views representation learning as a collective phenomenon in high-dimensional systems, bridging deterministic and stochastic regimes of gradient-based optimization.

title_en: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
abstract_en: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. title_en: COMBIO: Automated Discovery of a Compact Composite Biomarker from Routine Laboratory Panels
abstract_en: Machine-learning models based on routine laboratory panels can predict outcomes but can be difficult to interpret and operationalize. We present COMBIO, an automated pipeline that distils such a model into a compact closed-form biomarker. The composite is a product of laboratory measurements raised to integer powers from minus two to two. The sign of each exponent indicates whether higher values of the corresponding measurement increase or decrease the composite. The hospital mortality composite had an area under the curve of 0.698 in the external database. A version restricted to widely available measurements in the source hospital database achieved an area under the curve of 0.786 in a cohort covering 92% of admissions. The multiplicative representation provides compactness rather than additional accuracy, and local validation and recalibration are required before clinical use.

title_en: TUGB: A Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding Framework
abstract_en: Generative modeling, particularly Decision Transformers, shows promise in auto-bidding strategies. However, it struggles with limited exploration in static offline datasets, vulnerability to dynamic environmental shifts, and a reliance on heuristic return-to-go (RTG) specifications that may yield suboptimal performance on unseen traffic. To address these challenges, we propose the Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding (TUGB) framework. TUGB integrates generative sequence modeling with Reinforcement Learning (RL). Notably, full-scale deployment on JD Search Ad achieved a 2.32\% increase in cost and 3.57\% in target cost, validating its industrial efficacy, while its successful adaptation to subsequent mechanism upgrades and JD Food Delivery Ad further validates TUGB's superior generalization capability.

title_en: WearableBridge: Task-Guided Latent Transport for Free-Living Activity Recognition
abstract_en: Wrist-worn accelerometers make activity monitoring feasible at scale, but incidental arm motion, device orientation, and shifting context blur the signal that separates activities. Calibration studies supply higher-quality references such as concurrent thigh recordings or supervised laboratory wrist sessions, but they are expensive, cover few participants, and are rarely available at deployment. How can limited reference data improve recognition for participants who wear only a wrist device? We propose WearableBridge, which holds the reference encoder and classifier fixed and learns a task-guided transport map, the bridge, that carries each wrist feature into the region the classifier associates with its activity. Reference features or the classifier's predictions indicate the destination, and a classification loss penalizes wrist features that land in the region of another activity. We instantiate WearableBridge with three bridges: Mapper regresses onto reference features, Distillation matches the classifier's class probabilities, and MeanFlow learns a one-step flow from wrist toward reference features. On 40 held-out free-living PAAWS participants, all three bridges improve macro-F1 in every training run, and the strongest, MeanFlow, raises mean macro-F1 from 35.1% to 56.0% with concurrent thigh references (Thigh2Wrist), and from 54.0% to 63.5% with group-matched laboratory wrist references (Lab2Freeliving). Fitted only on PAAWS, MeanFlow also raises macro-F1 on the CAPTURE-24 cohort from 42.8% to 54.7%. The gains replicate on selfBACK, hold across four reference encoders, and grow with temporal context. A study can therefore collect reference recordings for a calibration subset and improve wrist-only recognition for every other participant, training only a bridge of 0.13 to 2.44 million parameters while the reference encoder and classifier stay unchanged.

title_en: StreamTab: Training-Free Temporal Link Prediction with Tabular Foundation Models
abstract_en: Temporal link prediction uses past interactions to predict whether two nodes will interact in the future. Temporal graph neural networks achieve strong results on this task, but they are trained separately for each graph. How a model should use interaction history also depends on the candidates it is compared with. A past interaction can distinguish a recurring link from a random pair that has never interacted, but when the negative candidates have also interacted before, other signals are needed. We propose StreamTab, a training-free framework built on a frozen tabular foundation model pretrained only on synthetic tables. StreamTab describes each candidate pair by statistics of its past interactions and shows the model recent observed interactions and sampled negative pairs as labeled examples, from which the model scores new candidates. Its central design, regime conditioning, samples the negative examples according to how the candidates are sampled, so the examples show the distinction the model must make. As new interactions arrive, StreamTab updates the statistics and refreshes the examples while the model parameters stay fixed. On thirteen datasets against 21 temporal graph baselines, StreamTab achieves the highest average precision on twelve datasets under historical sampling and eleven under inductive sampling, and ranks first or stays within one point of the best on seven datasets under random sampling. With the same features and model, regime conditioning raises average precision over examples with random negatives by a median of 12.6 points under historical sampling.

title_en: When Can You Trust Neural Critics? Auditing Mutual Information Estimates of Higher-Order Epistasis in Protein Language Models
abstract_en: Mutual information (MI) estimation is used to probe what neural representations encode, including in protein language models, but variational MI estimators have variance that scales at least exponentially in the true MI. We audit a prior neural-MI study of order-resolved epistasis in ESM-2 on the four-site GB1 landscape. Run-to-run differences show no systematic bias and a magnitude comparable to ordinary cross-seed retraining variability, and the evaluation-pairing scheme shifts scores substantially. At the original dimensionality, two of three alternative estimator families stabilize the estimate across seeds and one does not. In a synthetic calibration at the representation dimensionalities of two other protein language models (a Gaussian channel with known MI; no model representations), all three families recover materially less signal than required, despite correct signal ordering and stable seeds. A control critic given the true signal direction, which also reduces its input to one dimension, recovers 93.3% and 98.7% of the analytic MI at gain 1.5 (at 5,120 and 4,096 dimensions), so the signal is recoverable with privileged information, but the control does not identify why blind estimation fails. title_en: Function-Space Certification for Neural Operators
abstract_en: Certifying the robustness and physical consistency of scientific machine-learning models ensures that their predictions remain reliable beyond the test set. For neural operators, which learn PDE solution operators by mapping infinite-dimensional function spaces, certification means establishing rigorous, domain-wide guarantees for their output functions. However, standard neural network (NN) verification methods are fundamentally designed for vector-to-vector mappings, and they can only certify neural operators at fixed grid resolutions and provide no guarantees over the entire domain or across another resolution. We close this gap by introducing a function-space certification framework that verifies neural operators across the entire continuous domain. We formulate interval bound propagation (IBP) and CROWN in function space, propagating upper and lower bound functions through each layer using rigorous numerical integration. In addition, we extend bound propagation to higher-order derivatives to certify PDE residuals and solution error bounds. Experiments across several neural operator architectures and scientific problems, including the 572.5-million-parameter spherical Fourier neural operator for global weather forecasting, show that our method produces tight, domain-wide guarantees efficiently, providing a foundation for trustworthy operator learning.

title_en: DeepRT-Cal: Learning to Calibrate Ray-Traced Twin Channel Statistics with Low-Fidelity Environmental Geometry
abstract_en: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems increasingly rely on digital twin channels (DTCs) to represent and interact with physical radio environments. title_en: Optimal Probabilistic Answer Set Programming: Complexity and Implementations
abstract_en: Probabilistic Answer Set Programming (PASP) extends Answer Set Programming with the possibility of representing uncertain data. title_en: Capital Efficiency, Isolation, Risk, and Ruin in Generative AI Inference Serving Infrastructure
abstract_en: Generative AI serving is an extremely capital-intensive endeavor that demands rapid, step-change improvements in capital efficiency to prevent industry wide increases in the cost of capital from limiting growth plans. Keeping pace with the economic necessities will increasingly require infrastructure providers to confront operationally-inconvenient realities of production serving, including the extreme heterogeneity of generative AI request costs. We have explored workload isolation as a foundational, fleet-level lever for increasing capital efficiency. Isolation is the practice of intelligently grouping "like" requests before execution. Rather than exposing every replica to the full heterogeneous workload distribution, isolation deliberately reshapes the workload presented to the hardware by assigning requests with different cost characteristics to different portions of the fleet. Workload isolation on its own does not make expensive requests cheaper; it prevents a costly portion of the workload from unnecessarily determining the operating point and capital efficiency of the entire fleet. It additionally lays the foundational groundwork that can serve as a launching point for compounding gains via narrow-band optimizations (tailoring) and custom silicon designs while also informing up on pricing policy. This paper uses representative production data and experience to convey the motivation behind isolation as a fleet-level lever for increased capital efficiency.

title_en: Rethinking Optimization Methods for Hierarchical Feature Selection
abstract_en: Rare-event forecasting often depends on interpretable conjunctions: a single keyword, location, or temporal cue may be weak, while their joint occurrence can identify a meaningful precursor. Hierarchical-Task Numerical conjunctive feature Learning (HTNL) selects Numerical Conjunctive Features (NCFs) through a structured sparsity objective. However, the resulting optimization problem is challenging, making optimization design critical to its practical performance. We give a unified diagnosis of four HTNL optimization families: original majorization-minimization (MM), variational quadratic form (VQF), alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), and weighted group lasso (WGL). Our analysis distinguishes three key factors that jointly determine HTNL optimization behavior. First, VQF and MM are algebraically equivalent under matched variational updates and optimize a squared-penalty formulation. Second, ADMM optimizes the unsquared objective through consensus splitting; we replace its truncated FISTA proximal solver with a scalar bisection update (ADMM-Bisect) for more accurate treatment of near-threshold blocks. Third, WGL targets the same unsquared objective, while all methods face rapidly decaying active-set admission scores. Across two synthetic datasets and 11 civil-unrest and flu-surveillance tasks, VQF achieves the highest mean AUC with the most compact non-collapsing supports. ADMM-Bisect reduces measured runtime, while calibrated WGL avoids the empty-support failures of its original scale. Synthetic results further show how proximal accuracy, pruning, and search budget affect candidate recovery, especially for longer conjunctions. Code will be made publicly available upon publication.

title_en: Knowledge Distillation from Neural Networks to Differentiable Logic Networks
abstract_en: Differentiable logic networks (DLNs) are interpretable, edge-friendly classifiers that learn both their logic operators and their connections through gradient descent, achieving accuracy competitive with multi-layer perceptrons at orders-of-magnitude lower inference cost. Their accuracy, however, is bounded by the problems of vanishing gradients, scalability, and lack of an ecosystem, leaving a gap relative to conventional neural networks on several datasets. We introduce knowledge distillation for DLNs to narrow this gap. We distill from a trained multi-layer perceptron teacher into a DLN student, integrating the distillation objective into a two-phase training loop without altering the architecture or the inference procedure. The teacher is discarded after training. Hence, the distilled model retains the interpretability, sparsity, and inference cost of a conventionally trained DLN. We investigate this approach through four variants: a joint hyperparameter search that optimizes the distillation weight and temperature alongside the architecture, a grid search over these two hyperparameters with the architecture fixed, and two single-phase variants that employ distillation during only the neuron-function or only the connection phase. On 20 public tabular classification tasks, distillation improves balanced-class accuracy at negligible cost to gate-level operation counts and model size, though the benefit varies by dataset. Performance improvements of up to 15% are observed, in some cases surpassing the teacher itself.

title_en: Enforcing Symmetries on Pre-trained ML Models for Physics
abstract_en: Post-hoc group averaging (or test-time augmentation) is a simple way to impose symmetry on a trained predictor without changing its architecture or retraining it. For finite and compact groups, averaging over a normalized Haar measure on the group gives the Reynolds operator: a canonical projection onto invariant or equivariant predictors with known non-increasing risk guarantees under certain assumptions. This paper provides numerical experiments on physics emulation models that demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in this setting. We then extend this framework to non-compact group symmetries. For non-compact groups, the Haar measure cannot be normalized, so group averaging cannot be defined in the same way. We replace it with three alternatives: the Weyl unitary trick (which requires complexifying the space and extending the predictor), a data-dependent orthogonal projection (which involves a non-trivial optimization on the space of invariant or equivariant functions), and a frame averaging approach (which involves mapping each point to a set of orbit representatives). We illustrate the constructions theoretically and empirically on the unit-rescaling group and the Lorentz group. Our results show that in the non-compact case, the Weyl trick and frame averaging do not provide a consistent improvement over the baseline, except where the test data is out-of-distribution (an orders-of-magnitude improvement in this case) and, for the Weyl trick, in low-data regimes. The orthogonal projection can provide improvements in-distribution and out-of-distribution. We also observe that models trained directly on invariant features matched or beat the projection of an unconstrained one. We conclude that post-hoc symmetrization extends to non-compact groups, but it does not consistently outperform training a symmetric model.

title_en: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training
abstract_en: Quantization-aware training (QAT) is the most reliable way to obtain accurate low-bit large language models (LLMs), but training with AdamW keeps two dense FP32 states for every weight matrix. title_en: Ordered Policy Optimization
abstract_en: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) stabilizes policy updates by clipping the importance ratio between the new policy and the data-collecting policy. The standard rule uses one fixed clipping range for all samples. Motivated by this observation, we propose Ordered Policy Optimization (\textsc{OPO}). In each minibatch, \textsc{OPO} sorts the importance ratios, selects the extreme ratios that potentially have the largest effect on the update, and assigns them adaptive sample-wise radii instead of using the fixed clipping radius. These radii are derived from a prescribed tail profile, which specifies desired target values for the selected extreme ratios. The resulting objective remains first-order and requires only minibatch sorting and a modified policy loss. Experiments conducted on MuJoCo and Atari benchmarks demonstrate that this simple modification achieves strong performance relative to established baselines.

title_en: Accuracy Is Not Value: Choosing Weak Supervisors by What the Student Inherits
abstract_en: Weak supervisors are usually judged by their own errors, but what matters is what a student learns from them. For squared loss and any linear learner shared by all supervisors, we show that a supervisor's value is determined by its errors after they pass through the student's learning operator. Consequently, the inner products of the supervisors' raw errors can be compatible with every feasible value of the student's risk, and weighting supervisors by them can be arbitrarily worse than the best weighting in relative excess risk. This student-relative value is not identifiable from unlabeled data, but what is missing is small: one finite-dimensional projection of the target decides whether training on a weak aggregate helps, another decides how to weight the supervisors. Known teacher training rules, or a label-model condition stated in student-relative form, shrink it further. Clean labels close the remaining gap at a cost set by the geometry of the unresolved directions rather than by the dimension of the student's representation, with matching worst-case lower bounds. In Gaussian designs we also quantify when exact teacher structure beats ordinary stacking and when weak supervisors, combined with clean labels, beat every procedure that uses the clean labels alone. The guarantees extend to fitted ridge students and finite unlabeled data.

title_en: Surrogate Quality Score: A Novel Composite Performance Metric for Model Selection
abstract_en: The growing reliance on high-fidelity, state-of-the-art machine learning based models for engineering decision-making necessitates robust and systematic approaches for model selection. While high predictive accuracy at untrained points is a necessary trait in the final model, other attributes such as model complexity, forecastability, explainability, scalability, and physics-awareness may be equally important or relevant criteria depending on application context and user requirements. In this work, we propose a novel composite performance metric, Surrogate Quality Score (SQS) for model selection based on predictive accuracy and model complexity simultaneously. SQS heuristically integrates these two attributes through a weighted product of normalized measures, yielding a unified score to reflect overall model quality. We extensively discuss and justify the formulation of SQS and demonstrate its utility through an illustrative example. By combining predictive accuracy and model complexity, SQS offers a systematic and objective approach for model selection based on both attributes.

title_en: Who's Asking? Audience-Conditioned Privatization
abstract_en: The abundance of user-generated conversational data makes the question of how to responsibly derive insights from confidential data without putting the individuals in it at risk ever more important. However, the majority of existing differentially private (DP) synthetic text generation (SDG) and anonymization approaches ignore the context of the data's downstream usage, which results in loss of important information. They both ignore the observation that an attribute that is harmless to one audience can be sensitive to another, and each audience typically needs only some attributes preserved. On bioRxiv data, our SDG method improves MAUVE from 0.097 to 0.420 at epsilon=1 and on the proprietary real estate data, our anonymization method improves MAUVE from 0.698 to 0.959 over the best baselines.

title_en: The Relational Capacity Framework: A Lens for AI-Mediated Relationality
abstract_en: A growing literature examines the impact of engaging with AI chatbots on our relationality: our ability to form relationships with others, maintain them through life's changes, and exit when needed. title_en: Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline for Multi-Instance Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning
abstract_en: We present the Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline (ASP), an offline rollout scheduler for multi-instance asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) of large language models (LLMs). This enables efficient multi-instance rollout that overcomes the early scaling plateau of single-instance inference while reducing fluctuations in the supply of generated samples to the trainer. We integrate the scheduler into an asynchronous architecture that decouples rollout from training while keeping policy lag observable and bounded. Within our asynchronous architecture, ASP's scheduling reduces mean iteration time by 10.9%. The complete system improves end-to-end throughput by up to 3.22 times and reduces iteration time by up to 76.8% relative to MindSpeed-RL, while reducing iteration time by up to 62.5% relative to verl. It also scales more robustly with additional generation resources than these baselines and shows no visible convergence degradation in the measured bounded-lag regime. ASP has since been used in an internal telecom-domain RL post-training workflow, reducing the reported training period from more than three months to two months and producing a domain-enhanced model for knowledge answering and tool calling.
